title: Back button doesn't work with elements synced with query params
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When pressing the browser back button, the streamlit script does not reexecute, so elements synced with `st.query_params` do not refresh

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-13853)

```Python
import streamlit as st

num_elements = 10

st.set_page_config(page_title="Mock element Slider", layout="centered")

element_ids = [f"mock-element-{i:02d}" for i in range(num_elements)]
element_to_idx = {element_id: idx for idx, element_id in enumerate(element_ids)}

url_element_id = st.query_params.get("element_id")
if (
    "mock_element_id" not in st.session_state
    or st.session_state["mock_element_id"] not in element_to_idx
):
    st.session_state["mock_element_id"] = (
        url_element_id if url_element_id in element_to_idx else element_ids[0]
    )

with st.container(key="mock-element-slider"):
    st.select_slider(
        "element",
        options=element_ids,
        key="mock_element_id",
        label_visibility="collapsed",
    )

st.query_params["element_id"] = st.session_state["mock_element_id"]

current_element_id = st.session_state["mock_element_id"]
current_idx = element_to_idx[current_element_id]
with st.popover(f"element `{current_element_id}`"):
    st.markdown(f"({current_idx}/{num_elements})")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a streamlit app with the above code, and go to http://localhost:8501/?element_id=mock-element-3
2. Drag the element to mock-element-5
3. Press the browser back button. 

### Expected Behavior

You would expect the slider to go back to mock-element-3

### Current Behavior

The slider stays at mock-element-5

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

I've previously seen https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9279, which looks related but is different and doesn't resolve this issue

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-13853)
Marking as enhancement since this is currently expected. We'll figure out whether we want to change this behavior with the upcoming `bind` parameter, and maybe also for `st.query_params`.

This is a request for browser back/forward to restore widgets that are manually synced with `st.query_params`. Assigning query params uses `pushState` (`handlePageInfoChanged` in `App.tsx`), so the URL and history stack do change, but `onHistoryChange` is built around page navigation. On the same page it either does not produce a useful rerun, or it reruns with `getQueryString()` reading stale React `queryParams` instead of `document.location.search`. Even a correct rerun would not restore the slider here, because the keyed widget value in `st.session_state` is only initialized from the URL once. Maintainers already marked this as expected and want to revisit it with `bind="query-params"` (which currently uses `replaceState`, so it does not create history entries either).

### Related Issues

- [#13963](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13963): Same-page back/forward with `st.navigation` does rerun, but `st.query_params` stays stale. That report explicitly calls out this single-page case and traces the stale values to `getQueryString()` preferring React state over the restored URL.
- [#9279](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9279) (closed): Cross-page back navigation dropped query params on the first rerun. Cited by the reporter; fixed in PR #13129 via `preserveQueryParams`, which did not cover same-page query-param history.
- [#9325](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9325): Original request to bind widget/`session_state` values to query params. Relevant because restoring widgets from history is part of that binding/bookmarkability design, not just a one-off `popstate` fix.
